steps.body: A ruler is a whole stretched into a line: cut the distance from 0 to 1 into equal jumps and every mark earns a fraction name.
steps.narration: A ruler is a whole stretched into a line: cut the distance from 0 to 1 into equal jumps and every mark earns a fraction name.

widget.prompt: On an EIGHTHS ruler, place the mark that sits at 1/2.

commonPlacements.feedback: 1/8 is a single jump from 0 — one eighth of the way, not half.
8/8 is the far end of the ruler, a whole unit from zero.

widget.successFeedback: 4/8 — four of the eight equal jumps is exactly halfway, the same point as 1/2.
widget.lowFeedback: Jumps run FORWARD from 0, so a landing behind the target is short of it — count the jumps again.
widget.highFeedback: That overshoots halfway — four of the eight jumps is where 1/2 sits, so stop there.

predict.prompt: On an eighths ruler, does any mark land exactly on 1/2?
predict.reveal: Eight is even, so half the jumps is a whole number of jumps: 4/8 lands precisely on 1/2.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f ruler really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f ruler comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

explanationVariants: Half the jumps is half the trip.

widget.prompt: On a ruler marked in eighths, which mark lands exactly on 1/2?

options.label: The 4/8 mark
options.feedback: Correct — four of the eight equal jumps is half the trip, so 4/8 and 1/2 name the same point.

options.label: The 2/8 mark
options.feedback: 2/8 is only a quarter of the way — two jumps out of eight, not four.

options.label: The 1/8 mark
options.feedback: 1/8 is a single jump from zero, nowhere near the halfway point of eight jumps.

options.label: There is no such mark
options.feedback: Eighths do land on a half: because 8 is even, the midpoint falls exactly on a mark.

commonErrors.feedback: The bottom was multiplied by 4, so the top must be too — otherwise the value changes.
Renaming SCALES both numbers; adding 4 to the top breaks the ratio.

widget.prompt: A trail is 4/6 mile, then 1/6 mile more. Express the total as ?/6. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 names the piece size; adding same-size pieces changes only how MANY you have.
Multiplying the counts is not joining them — 4 pieces and 1 more pieces make 5.
